detail:
The National Psoriasis Foundation describes funded research asking how skin inflammation and joint inflammation are connected in psoriatic arthritis, a link that remains poorly understood even though a substantial share of people with psoriasis eventually develop arthritis, often years after the skin disease begins. One active project it funds uses an in vivo proteomics system together with human patient samples to map the network of proteins secreted from inflamed skin that travel to the joints.

The project's stated aim is to identify specific skin-derived proteins that switch on synovial macrophages, the immune cells lining the joint, and drive joint inflammation. Work of this kind reflects a broader direction the Foundation describes: finding the biological signals that predict which people with psoriasis will develop joint disease, so that a clinically useful diagnostic test and earlier, more targeted treatments become possible.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about psoriatic arthritis research.
sourceVideoTitle: NPF-Funded Research: Characterization of Skin-To-Joint Communication Pathways in Psoriatic Arthritis
summary: A National Psoriasis Foundation-funded project maps proteins secreted from inflamed skin that travel to joints and activate joint-lining immune cells, seeking the signals that link psoriasis to psoriatic arthritis.
takeaways: researchers are mapping skin-to-joint protein signals
joint-lining macrophages are a focus of the work
a long-term goal is predicting who develops joint disease
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Where psoriatic arthritis research is heading
